faq.q: Can this download Instagram photos or videos?
faq.a: No, and the tool says so directly. A web page can't download Instagram media — Instagram requires you to be logged in, blocks cross-origin access, and prohibits scraping in its Terms of Service. To export your own content, use Instagram's official 'Download Your Information' feature in Accounts Center. The toolkit covers the parts of the workflow that genuinely work in-browser.

faq.q: Why does the caption formatter add invisible characters?
faq.a: Instagram collapses consecutive blank lines, so your paragraph spacing disappears when you paste. The formatter inserts a zero-width space (U+200B) on each empty line so the spacing survives. It also counts characters against the 2,200 caption limit and copies the formatted version for you.

faq.q: What Instagram sizes does the image resizer export, and what's the safe-area guide?
faq.a: It exports Square 1080×1080, Portrait 1080×1350, Landscape 1080×566 and Story/Reel 1080×1920. You choose 'Crop to fill' or 'Letterbox (fit)', and JPEG or PNG with a quality slider. For the 1920-tall story format, a 'safe-area guide' shades the top (~250px) and bottom (~310px) UI zones so you don't place text where Instagram's interface covers it.

faq.q: How does the hashtag manager and bio builder work?
faq.a: The hashtag manager has curated niche sets (study, motivation, travel, fitness, etc.), a 30-tag counter, a 'Remove Duplicates' button, and lets you save custom sets to your browser's localStorage. The bio builder enforces the 150-character limit, preserves line breaks, and shows a checklist (fits 150 chars, uses line breaks, has an emoji, mentions a link). A 3-column grid planner lets you drag images to preview your feed.
